title: Mentioning the specific name of the lending institution may predict slower funding for women.
Broad aspirational language regarding social service may predict slower funding for men, suggesting a gender interaction.
Female borrowers who mention marital status, number of children, or personal hardships fund more slowly.
Female borrowers over the age of 50 may fund faster than younger female borrowers.
Female borrowers who express confidence or determination regarding loan repayment may fund faster.
Including specific details about age, region, or family is associated with slower funding for women but faster funding for men.
The use of standardized boilerplate phrasing regarding the reduction of health and hazard risks may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
For female borrowers, increased pitch length may correlate with faster funding, contradicting the general trend.
Male borrowers who make explicit promises of timely repayment may fund more slowly.
Mentioning the specific number of children may predict slower funding for female borrowers.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention securing the future of their family fund faster.
Providing specific operational or inventory details predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Detailed inventory lists have opposite effects on funding speed for men and women.
